title: Unlocking Wide‐Temperature Battery States via Noninvasive Nonlinear Ultrasound
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) are central to modern energy storage, yet evaluating their internal states under extreme thermal fluctuations remains a critical challenge. Here we present a non‐destructive evaluation framework that leverages the quasi‐static component (QSC) of nonlinear ultrasonic guided waves. By integrating an operando electro‐acoustic‐thermal platform, we isolate temperature‐induced artefacts from intrinsic acoustic signals. This statistical compensation enables the precise, simultaneous prediction of state of charge (SOC) and state of charge relative to nominal capacity (SOC N ) across a wide temperature span (−10°C to 40°C). Furthermore, in situ multidimensional characterization maps these ultrasonic signatures to temperature‐dependent mechanics and irreversible capacity fade mechanisms. Ultimately, this unified framework provides a scalable, quantitative diagnostic tool for reliable energy systems operating under extreme environments.
title_zh: Unlocking Wide‐Temperature Battery States via Noninvasive Nonlinear Ultrasound

title: Physics‐Informed Meta‐Learning With Graph Attention for Lithium‐Ion Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction
abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate prediction of lithium‐ion battery (LIB) remaining useful life (RUL) is important for assessing battery degradation and supporting reliable operation of energy systems. However, prediction across different operating conditions remains challenging because of complex spatial–temporal dependencies, limited degradation observations, and difficulties in incorporating degradation‐related physical knowledge. To overcome these challenges, this study presents a physics‐informed meta‐graph attention network (PIMGAN) that integrates degradation feature learning, dynamical regularization, and few‐shot adaptation. Firstly, a multi‐scale graph attention mechanism is combined with adaptive bidirectional temporal convolution to characterize correlations among heterogeneous battery measurements and their temporal evolution. Then, a physics‐guided regulator (PGR) learns a nonlinear differential operator in the latent feature space, whose residual serves as an additional regularization term during model training. Finally, a first‐order meta‐learning strategy is integrated to learn transferable model initialization parameters across multiple degradation tasks, enabling rapid adaptation to unseen battery conditions with limited target‐domain observations while avoiding explicit second‐order meta‐gradient computations. The proposed PIMGAN is evaluated on two publicly available LIB datasets under cross‐cycle and cross‐condition prediction settings. Under cross‐condition evaluation, PIMGAN achieves mean absolute percentage errors of 0.267% and 0.336% on the MIT and XJTU datasets, respectively, demonstrating its effectiveness in battery RUL prediction with limited target‐domain data.
title_zh: Physics‐Informed Meta‐Learning With Graph Attention for Lithium‐Ion Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction

title: Co-optimization of intraday and frequency containment reserve bids for battery energy storage
abstract: As renewable energy integration increases supply variability, battery energy storage systems (BESS) present a viable solution for balancing supply and demand. This paper proposes a joint bidding strategy that combines participation in the primary frequency reserve market with continuous trading in the intraday market, addressing a gap in the extant literature that typically considers these markets in isolation and simplifies the continuous nature of intraday trading. Our approach utilizes a mixed integer linear programming implementation of the rolling intrinsic algorithm for intraday decisions and state of charge recovery, alongside a learned classifier strategy (LCS) that determines optimal day-ahead capacity allocation between markets. A comprehensive out-of-sample backtest over more than one year of tick level historical German market data validates our approach: The LCS increases overall profits by over 4\% compared to the best-performing static strategy and by more than 3\% over a naive dynamic benchmark. Crucially, our method closes the gap to a theoretical perfect foresight strategy to just 4\%, demonstrating the effectiveness of dynamic, learning-based allocation in a complex, multi-market environment.
title_zh: Co-optimization of intraday and frequency containment reserve bids for battery energy storage

title: Electric vehicle–integrated sustainable community microgrids: A review of control strategies, challenges, opportunities and pathways toward SDG 7
abstract: The demand for electricity continues to increase with economic growth and increasing end-use electrification, particularly in the transport sector. Despite ongoing progress, achieving Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7 by 2030, which aims to provide affordable and clean energy for all, remains uneven and structurally constrained. Electric vehicle (EV)-integrated community microgrids (MGs), operating in grid-connected or islanded modes are a promising solution that combines distributed energy resources, local electricity generation options and mobile energy storage systems (ESSs) through EV fleets. However, the high penetration of renewable energy resources, EVs and battery ESSs introduces significant challenges to system stability, power flow and operational reliability. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of recent developments in EV-integrated community MGs, energy management, decentralized EV fleet coordination and bidirectional EV charging/discharging into the electricity network. It also provides a framework for integrating MGs, EVs, and renewables, including grid-to-vehicle (G2V) charging, bidirectional vehicle-to-grid (V2G) and vehicle-to-everything (V2X) applications, to enhance grid flexibility and ancillary services. It further discusses the optimization mechanisms, control frameworks and their applications within the MG environment. In addition, the review evaluates the contribution of EV-integrated community MGs toward achieving SDG 7 in sustainable community energy systems. The analysis also addresses existing technical, economic, social acceptance and regulatory challenges that hinder large-scale deployments. The study outlines future research directions and proposes a conceptual framework for researchers and policymakers, offering actionable pathways to accelerate the global clean energy transition and support the achievement of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
title_zh: Electric vehicle–integrated sustainable community microgrids: A review of control strategies, challenges, opportunities and pathways toward SDG 7

title: A Review of State-of-Health Estimation and Prediction Methods for Lithium-Ion Traction Batteries in Vehicular Applications: Task Definition, Benchmark Evaluation, and Deployment Challenges
abstract: The state of health (SOH) of traction batteries is a common basis for safety warning, residual value assessment, and second-life utilization of electric vehicles, but a gap exists between the laboratory accuracy of existing deep learning methods and their on-board usability. This paper reviews the relevant research progress using on-board usability as the screening criterion. SOH estimation, SOH prediction, and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction are distinguished according to label source and evaluation protocol, and the limits on the comparability of error values are explained. Existing methods are grouped into six categories by modeling mechanism and evaluated category by category using four on-board questions: input availability, cross-domain generalization validation, uncertainty output, and edge-computing resource constraints. Six models are compared on the CALCE CS2 dataset under random splitting, temporal extrapolation, and cell-level holdout protocols. Under random splitting, the mean absolute errors of all six models do not exceed 0.0150. Under temporal extrapolation, they range from 0.0204 to 0.1392, and the R² values of three neural networks become negative. Under cell-level holdout, they range from 0.0254 to 0.0378. Under the CALCE CS2 dataset and the settings of this paper, protocol selection changes both the error level and the model ranking.
title_zh: A Review of State-of-Health Estimation and Prediction Methods for Lithium-Ion Traction Batteries in Vehicular Applications: Task Definition, Benchmark Evaluation, and Deployment Challenges
